#### 1. otofaciocervical syndrome 1  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.836)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:3519)

**Proposed mechanism:** EYA1 (HGNC:3519) —DISRUPTS→ EYA1-SOX10 transcriptional regulation; EYA1 (HGNC:3519) —BINDS→ SOX10 (HGNC:11056); SOX10 (HGNC:11056) —BINDS→ EYA1-SOX10 transcriptional regulation; EYA1-SOX10 transcriptional regulation —LEADS_TO→ Branchial arch development; EYA1-SOX10 transcriptional regulation —LEADS_TO→ Otic placode development; EYA1-SOX10 transcriptional regulation —LEADS_TO→ Cervical somite development; Branchial arch development —LEADS_TO→ Branchial cleft anomalies (HP:0000377); Otic placode development —LEADS_TO→ External ear malformations (HP:0000384); Otic placode development —LEADS_TO→ Conductive hearing impairment (HP:0000390); Cervical somite development —LEADS_TO→ Cervical vertebral fusion (HP:0001266). **How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in EYA1 with a consistent loss-of-function effect in both diseases would support this hypothesis. Conversely, if variants associated with one disease consistently show gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects, or if EYA1 variants are absent in affected individuals of one disease group, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: N/A)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis and developmental pathways affected by EYA1 mutations can inform diagnostic strategies and potentially identify therapeutic targets for both branchiootorenal syndrome and otofaciocervical syndrome 1. For instance, interventions aimed at supporting branchial arch or otic placode development might offer therapeutic benefit.
